buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Payment

PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND WAGES: Service Provider is required to pay Salaries / wages of contracted staff deployed at buyer location first i.e. on their own and then claim payment from Buyer alongwith all statutory documents like, PF, ESIC etc. as well as the bank statement of payment done to staff. 3. Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) SECTION – IV SCOPE OF WORK 1. Introduction: The Call Centre of Animal Resource Development Department was established under the Livestoc k Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) with the 1962 toll-free helpline as a dedicated p latform for livestock owners to report animal health issues and seek timely veterinary assistance. Calls received through 1962 are used for prompt coordination and dispatch of Mobile Veterinary U nits (MVUs) for doorstep veterinary services, particularly in remote and underserved areas. The Call Centre also facilitates effective communication, monitoring and coordination among livest ock owners, MVUs and the Department, thereby supporting timely delivery of veterinary services and strengthening the implementation of LHDCP. 2. Name of Work: Running of the operation of “Call Centre” through deployment of suitable manpower. 3. Scope of Work: The ARD Call Centre (herein after called Helpdesk), established under the Animal Resources Development Department (ARD Department), shall operate from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM on all seven days of the week, inclu ding Saturdays, Sundays and Government holidays, except on such occasions as may be decided by the c ompetent authority. The Call Centre shall function as a ‘citizen-centric platform’ for providing information r elating to the “Animal in Distress” and “Animal Mobile Veterinary Ambulance” services, schemes and prog rammes of the ARD Department, Government of West Bengal. The Call Centre shall receive calls from the public, register and categorize their queries/service requests, p rovide appropriate information and assistance in a structured manner, and facilitate necessary coordinatio n for delivery of services. It shall also include development, operation and maintenance of an appropriate portal and/or customized/customizable software for efficient dissemination of information, registration, tra cking and management of citizen service requests. 3.1. Purpose: The purpose of the Helpdesk is to: - · Facilitating Veterinary Services through toll-free helpline ‘1962’. · Technical Assessment and MVU Dispatch for emergency treatment at farmers door step. · Monitoring, Coordination and Service Tracking. · Establish better feedback mechanism. · Dissemination citizen centric information.

3.2. The following services are to be provided: - A. Deployment of trained Call Centre Executive: The agency will have to deploy well trained Ca ll Centre Executives. Necessary program/ scheme specific training will be imparted by the Agency. The manpower deployed at the Helpdesk should have the following skill sets and qualities as menti oned in the clause No. 6 of Section-IV. B. Generation of MIS: The agency will have to produce dynamic MIS as demanded by the Departm ent time to time. 4. Civil and Electrical Infrastructure: Animal Resources Development Department will provide room, electricity, toll free Telephone Bills and fur niture (table, chair etc.) in office premise. The Animal Resources Development Department shall also provide necessary PRI Numbers and pay the re ntal charges for the same. 5. Process of Work: This procedure is applied to all Call Centre Executives and Veterinary Doctors involved in managing inbou nd calls from animal owners seeking advice or reporting animal health concerns. 5.1. The functions, roles and responsibilities of Call Centre: - Position Responsibility Call Centre Executives · Receive and log calls from animal owners. · Assess the health issue based on the caller’s description. · Provide immediate advice where possible or direct the caller to the Veterinarian. · Record details accurately in the system. · Maintain confidentiality and professionalis m in all interactions. · Oversee Call Centre operations. · Monitors call quality. · Handle escalations when necessary. · Ensure adherence to SOP and customer s ervice standards.

Veterinary Team · Review complex cases or provide remote consultations to callers when required. · Assist Call Centre executives in handling complicated or high-risk health issues. 6. Manpower at Call Centre: - A centralized Call Centre established with a dedicated toll-free number “1962”. The Call Centre has a well- trained and dedicated manpower and robust technical solutions required for running the Call Centre from 9 .00 AM to 6.00 PM for 365 days. Adequate persons have been deployed for attending phone calls with the knowledge of different languages like Bengali, Hindi and English. The Call Centre will be operated with thre e (3) Veterinarians, nine (9) Call Executives. 6.1. Engagement of Veterinarian: a. Engagement of Veterinary Officer on contractual basis through Interview with representation of DAH &VS, WB. b. Selection Committee shall prepare Panel of Veterinary Officer on the basis of merit and Panel will be valid for one year (01 Year) so that no unit would remain non-operational due to want of man pow er. (i) Selection Committee for Veterinary Officer: (a) DAH&VS, WB or his authorised representative ......................Chairman (b) Any officers nominated by DAH & VS, WB............Member (c) Representative of the implementing agency............Member (ii) Selection Committee for Call Executive: (a) Addl. Director, ARD or his authorised representative............Chairman (b) Any Technical officer nominated by DAH&VS, WB............Member (c) Representative of the Service Provider............Member c. Eligibility Criteria for Veterinary Officer: Criteria Suggested requirement Educational Qualification B.V.Sc & A.H. degree from a recognized veterinary institution.

Age The maximum serving age as a veterinarian– 70 years (if the applicant i s in good physical and mental health), on attaining the maximum age li mit he/she will be treated as stands released on the last day of the very month of his/her birth, except if the date falls on 1st day of a given mon th, he/she will be released on the last date of the preceding month. Registration Valid registration with the State Veterinary Council/VCI, as applicable. V CI registration requirements include a recognized veterinary degree an d State Veterinary Council registration. Experience Preferably 1-2 years’ professional experience in veterinary clinical servi ces/animal health. Experience in MVU, emergency veterinary services, helpline/call-centre or field veterinary services may be preferred. Clinical knowledge Sound knowledge of veterinary medicine, surgery, obstetrics & gynaec ology, preventive healthcare, vaccination, disease surveillance and zoo notic diseases. Call-centre competency Ability to assess information received from Call Executives and categori ze/prioritize cases according to urgency. MVU coordination Ability to determine the requirement and urgency of MVU deployment a nd coordinate with the concerned MVU/field veterinary institution. Tele-veterinary support Capable of providing appropriate preliminary/online veterinary advi ce to livestock owners and field personnel within the permissible scope of tele-advice. Language Good command of Bengali and English; knowledge of Hindi may be desi rable. Computer proficiency Working knowledge of web-based applications, case-management soft ware, GIS/GPS-based MVU tracking and digital reporting. Communication skills Good listening, counselling, decision-making and emergency-response skills. Monitoring & follow-up Ability to monitor pending cases, ensure follow-up and verify closure of service requests. d. Eligibility Criteria for Call Executive: Criteria Suggested requirement Educational Qualification Minimum Higher Secondary (10+2) pass from a recognized Board; Grad uate preferred. Age Preferably 18–40 years, with relaxation as per applicable Government n orms, if adopted. Data-entry skill Minimum 30 w.p.m. typing speed in English and adequate Bengali typin g/data-entry capability.

Relevant Experience Preferably 1–2 years’ experience in a call centre/customer-care/helpdes k/data-entry environment. Experience in Government/healthcare/anima l husbandry helpline may be given preference. Clinical knowledge Clinical knowledge regarding animal health along with certificate course of one/two year on Animal Husbandry practices may be preferred. Key functional competency Ability to accurately record caller details, animal details, location/GPS-r elated information, nature of emergency, contact number and other par ticulars in the Call Centre software. Language proficiency Bengali and English; ability to communicate effectively with rural livest ock owners. Knowledge of Hindi may be desirable. Computer proficiency Minimum 6-month Certificate/Diploma in Computer Application or equiv alent practical proficiency in MS Office, internet, data entry and web-ba sed applications. Communication skills Good verbal communication, active listening, patience and ability to ha ndle distressed/urgent callers professionally. Coordination Ability to coordinate with the Call Centre Veterinarian, MVU, local Veteri nary institution and field officials and follow escalation protocols. 7. Features of the Help-Desk: - The system has a capacity of handling multiple calls during peak time per day. The Call Centre has all the l atest features like call routing as per the skills, call recording for future requirement and quality monitoring , call barging Automatic Call Distributor (ACD) with dynamic queuing. IVR with intelligent routing, integrati on with database, call back scheduling, rule based dialing, etc. The Call Executives have excellent knowled ge of various dialects of the respective Local Language as per scope and communication skills so that the Call Executives can communicate and understand the queries of people easily. The Department has the rig ht to evaluate the Call Executives at any stage and can release them in case they are not found suitable. U nder such circumstances, the Service Provider have to replace the Call Executives within one week. The Call Centre is capable of receiving queries / complaints of all descriptions from the animal owner/anim al lovers over telephone. High Speed Internet Connectivity has been provided as per requirement. The animal owner/animal lovers may call from a mobile phone or land line alike. Caller Identification Syste m facilities has been provided for registering the number of the caller in the software. The identity of each caller is validated and registered by making query from the Call Executive attending the call centre; each a nd every validated query /complaint is registered in the application software. 8. Facilities & Equipments of Call Centre: - · Desktop PCs with dialing facilities for incoming & outgoing for each seat. · Secured Server space / Web spaces storage to save the captured data and local server for dialing facility. · Software required–Web based CRM software, dialing software.

· Local Area Network. · Appropriate no. of terminals from tele-service provider’s connection to the local server. · Required no. of telephone instruments of appropriate technology. · Call transfer Facility on Telephone sets. · Good Quality Headphones for each operator. · IVRS. · PRI cards & Modems 9. Services & Support by Tele Caller Provider: - · The telephone line of the Helpdesk is linked / mapped with a pre-defined number i.e. 033-2341-67 00 for which tie-up with BSNL is provided. Hunting facility is inbuilt so that at any point of time, an incoming call can land on one of the free lines (1962 / 1800-345-5573). The configuration of the nu mber is such that it is easy to remember. · It is always ensured that the same telephone number (033-2341-6700) is displayed as Caller Line Identification (CLI) in respect of all outgoing calls originating from any of the terminals of the Help desk to facilitate easy recognition by the ARD Department Officials. 10. Services offered: - · The Call Centre (Helpline number: 1962; 1800-3455-573) started its operation in West Bengal und er NADCP scheme in the FY2022-23 for monitoring of vaccination programmes. · As per the scheme mandate of ESVHD-MVU under LHDCP, 218 MVUs started operating in this Stat e in April’23 and since then, the Call Centre unit was entrusted to manage on-calls demand of ani mal owners towards discharge of emergency animal health care services at farmers’ doorstep thro ugh these MVUs. · Working hours of Call Centre: From 9.00 AM to 6.00 PM · Working days for Call Centre: 365 days · Daily timing for transferring the calls to the MVUs from the Call Centre: From 9.00 AM to 4.00 PM ( i.e. 7 hours every day) · Calls coming after 4.00 PM are listed at top on the next day and disposed of on priority basis on t he next day. 11. Procedure of call: - I. Call Reception: Step 1: Answer the Call · The call should be answered within 3 rings. · Greet the caller professionally with a welcoming tone. Step 2: Verify Caller Information · Collect the caller’s name, phone number, and the animal’s details (species, breed, age, etc.).

· Record the information in the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system to create or upd ate a caller’s profile. Step 3: Understand the Health Concern · Ask open-ended questions to understand the nature of the animal’s health issue. · Document the description of symptoms and any previous medical history provided. II. Assess the Situation: Step 4: Categorize the Issue Classify the issue based on urgency (e.g., emergency, urgent, routine): · Emergency: Severe injury, bleeding, difficulty breathing, collapse, etc. · Urgent: Symptoms indicating serious health concerns, like vomiting, fever, or lethargy, etc. · Routine: Minor health issues or general health inquiries (e.g., vaccination, diet recommendations), etc. Step 5: Provide Preliminary Advice · For non-urgent cases, provide basic first aid advice if applicable: · For urgent or emergency cases, direct the caller to the nearest veterinary clinic or animal hospital , ensuring the caller understands the severity. Step 6: Escalate to Veterinary Team, if required · If the call requires professional evaluation or the agent is unsure of the correct advice, escalate to a registered veterinarian or schedule a consultation. III. Call Closure: Step 7: Summarize the Call · Recap the advice given and ensure the caller understands the next steps. · Provide additional contact information if required (e.g. follow-up procedures). · If applicable, reschedule an appointment or follow-up call. Step 8: Close the Call · Politely close the call: · End the call courteously, ensuring the caller feels reassured. IV. Documentation and Reporting: Step 9: Record the Interaction · Ensure all information related to the call (caller details, animal health issue, advice given, etc.) is accurately logged into the CRM system. · Document any follow-up required and set reminders for follow-up calls if necessary. Step 10: Monitor and Track Trends · Regularly analyze call data to identify common health concerns or recurring issues.

· Provide feedback to the veterinary team or Supervisor based on trends. Escalation Procedures:- Emergency Cases: · Direct the caller to approach to the nearest veterinary hospital immediately. · If necessary, initiate an urgent dispatch of an emergency responder [e.g., Mobile Veterinary Unit ( MVU) for animals]. Unresolved or Complex Cases: · Escalate the case to the Veterinary Doctors of Call Centre for a remote consultation. Complaint or Dissatisfaction: · If a caller expresses dissatisfaction with the service, politely acknowledge their concern and escal ate the issue to the Veterinary Doctors. Performance Monitoring and Quality Assurance:- Monitoring: Supervisor should randomly listen to call recordings or monitor live calls to ensure compliance with the SOP, professionalism, and appropriate service levels. Feedback: Call Centre Executives should regularly receive feedback from supervisors regarding their perform ance, with areas for improvement identified. Training: Regular training sessions will be held to update staff on animal health issues, communication skills , and call handling procedures. Health and Safety Protocols:- • Ensure Call Executives, Supervisor and Veterinary Doctors work in a clean, ergonomic environm ent. • Follow all organizational protocols regarding health and safety in the workplace. • Call Centre Executives must maintain a calm and supportive demeanour, especially when discus sing animal health emergencies, to provide reassurance to distressed callers. Confidentiality and Data Protection: - •Ensure all information regarding animal health issues is kept confidential. •Adhere to data protection regulations to protect the personal information of both the caller and th e animal. Monitoring the Call Centre Activity: - The overall functioning of the ARD Call Centre shall be monitored by the Directorate of Animal Resources & Animal Health, West Bengal, through a designated Nodal Officer. The Nodal Officer shall oversee the day-to-day functioning of the Call Centre, performance of the service provider, call handling, registration a nd disposal of service requests, MVU coordination and maintenance of records.

A Veterinary Doctor/Group Leader shall be deployed at the Call Centre for technical supervision of animal- health-related calls, prioritization of cases, veterinary advice, escalation of emergency cases and coordinat ion with the concerned MVUs/field veterinary establishments. The service provider shall furnish daily opera tional data and monthly performance reports in the prescribed format for review by the Directorate. The c ompetent authority shall have the right to periodically review the performance of the Call Centre and issue necessary directions for improvement of service delivery. 4. Procedure of call: - I. Call Reception: Step 1: Answer the Call · The call should be answered within 3 rings. · Greet the caller professionally with a welcoming tone. · Record the information in the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system to create or upd ate a caller’s profile. Step 3: Understand the Health Concern · Ask open-ended questions to understand the nature of the animal’s health issue. · Document the description of symptoms and any previous medical history provided. II. Assess the Situation: Step 4: Categorize the Issue Classify the issue based on urgency (e.g., emergency, urgent, routine): · Emergency: Severe injury, bleeding, difficulty breathing, collapse, etc. · Urgent: Symptoms indicating serious health concerns, like vomiting, fever, or lethargy, etc. · Routine: Minor health issues or general health inquiries (e.g., vaccination, diet recommendations), etc. Step 5: Provide Preliminary Advice · For non-urgent cases, provide basic first aid advice if applicable: · For urgent or emergency cases, direct the caller to the nearest veterinary clinic or animal hospital , ensuring the caller understands the severity. Step 6: Escalate to Veterinary Team, if required · If the call requires professional evaluation or the agent is unsure of the correct advice, escalate to a registered veterinarian or schedule a consultation. III. Call Closure: Step 7: Summarize the Call · Recap the advice given and ensure the caller understands the next steps. · Provide additional contact information if required (e.g. follow-up procedures). · If applicable, reschedule an appointment or follow-up call. Step 8: Close the Call · Politely close the call: · End the call courteously, ensuring the caller feels reassured. IV. Documentation and Reporting: Step 9: Record the Interaction · Ensure all information related to the call (caller details, animal health issue, advice given, etc.) is accurately logged into the CRM system. · Document any follow-up required and set reminders for follow-up calls if necessary. · Provide feedback to the veterinary team or Supervisor based on trends.
